events.continuity_hook: Begins a short family travel episode after Tessa’s December work conference is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the Boise-area hotel zones, identify a practical two-night room setup, weigh driving versus a backup flight plan, and flag breakfast, parking, late-arrival food, and cancellation timing before Tessa places a hold.
events.scenario_brief: After the early-December conference, Tessa starts planning a late-January Boise weekend for her teenager’s club volleyball tournament, with a possible Sunday visit to relatives in Meridian. The family expects to drive from Salt Lake City on Friday after school, but winter road conditions on I-84 could make a late arrival uncomfortable. The team hotel near the tournament venue is convenient but has limited two-queen rooms and no included breakfast, while a Meridian hotel has breakfast and easier dinner options but adds morning drive time. The unresolved choices are whether to hold the team block, choose the Meridian option, and how late Friday departure can safely be.

events.continuity_hook: Finalizes the Boise family weekend after the tournament times and road concerns become clearer.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the hotel to book, set the Friday drive and late-check-in plan, identify a breakfast fallback if the schedule starts too early, and decide when to cancel any backup room.
events.scenario_brief: The tournament schedule is released: Saturday check-in is now early in Nampa, Sunday bracket play may run into midafternoon, and Tessa’s family cannot leave Salt Lake City until after a Friday school commitment. Forecasts also show possible blowing snow around Twin Falls. The team block releases soon, the downtown backup has become more expensive, and the Meridian breakfast-included hotel still has a cancellable two-queen room. The remaining decision is whether to accept the longer Saturday morning drive in exchange for easier meals and a safer cancellation setup.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the first spring yield travel episode after the brief family weekend planning is wrapped.
events.interaction_goal: Map the route order, compare flight windows, evaluate rental car versus rideshare, and shortlist hotel areas with included breakfast, parking clarity, and dinner access.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa opens a late-February Puget Sound admitted-student and transfer trip anchored by a Monday evening reception in Tacoma, a Tuesday midday transfer fair in Bellevue, a Tuesday night alumni-hosted dinner in Seattle, and a Wednesday counselor lunch in Everett. Salt Lake City to Seattle has several nonstop choices, but Monday arrival could be tight if traffic or baggage delays stack up. Hotel choices are split between staying near Tacoma the first night, using Bellevue as a two-night base, or moving north before the Everett lunch. The unresolved pieces are whether to arrive Sunday afternoon or Monday morning, whether to rent a car, and which hotel sequence keeps meals and morning drives manageable.

events.continuity_hook: Refines the Puget Sound plan after venue times and hotel availability shift.
events.interaction_goal: Rank Tacoma, Bellevue, South Lake Union, and north-end hotel options; list breakfast start times, parking charges, cancellation dates, and late-evening food choices; and identify the lowest-risk overnight sequence.
events.scenario_brief: The Puget Sound hosts tighten the timing: Tacoma registration now begins before the reception, the Bellevue transfer fair has an earlier exhibitor check-in, and the Seattle alumni dinner is confirmed near South Lake Union. Downtown Seattle rooms are filling because of a convention, while Tacoma and Bellevue still have practical cancellable options. Tessa needs to decide whether the first night should stay in Tacoma, whether Bellevue is worth the higher parking cost for the second night, and whether a north-end hotel would make Wednesday easier but Tuesday dinner harder.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Puget Sound plan from a narrowed route into reservations.
events.interaction_goal: Select the flight set, rental-car timing, hotel sequence, and room details; note window-seat requests, receipt items, breakfast logistics, dinner options, and final cancellation deadlines.
events.scenario_brief: Airfare and room holds are now bookable for the Puget Sound trip. A Sunday afternoon Salt Lake City to Seattle nonstop gives Tessa time to pick up a rental car and reach Tacoma before dinner, while the Monday morning flight is cheaper but leaves little cushion before the reception. For the return, a Wednesday midafternoon Seattle departure works after the Everett lunch; the later flight is cheaper but creates a long airport wait. Tacoma and Bellevue hotel holds expire that evening, and the rental-car rate has dropped enough to make driving between venues simpler than rideshares.

events.continuity_hook: Handles a final Puget Sound timing change after the main reservations are in place.
events.interaction_goal: Set the Tuesday night and Wednesday morning timeline, decide the luggage plan, confirm breakfast and checkout timing, plan fuel and rental-car return, and preserve a reasonable airport buffer.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before departure, the Wednesday counselor lunch is moved from Everett to Lynnwood, and Tessa’s return flight is retimed about half an hour earlier. Her Sunday flight, rental car, Tacoma hotel, and Bellevue hotel are already booked, but the final morning now has less slack. The unresolved choice is whether to keep the Bellevue hotel and drive north after checkout, switch the final night to a Lynnwood-area hotel while cancellation is still possible, or keep the current room and bring luggage directly to the lunch before heading to the airport.
